# What is the 'AI bubble' and what happens if it pops?

By Greta Reich, USA TODAY USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect

U.S. based AI company Anthropic, maker of popular chatbot Claude, filed for its initial public offering (IPO) on Oct. 26, giving the public a first official look into its business operations and ownership. [...] The paperwork Anthropic filed on Monday is only their registration statement to go public. They are expected to start trading before Thanksgiving, which will serve as a litmus test for investor demand and set the stage for other private AI companies, including OpenAI.

If Anthropic is overvalued, the AI bubble will continue to grow, creating a bigger fallout if it pops, according to Kelleher.

#### Why “Together” Matters

The scoring is useful. The conversation is where the value is. [...] Those projects weren’t killed by the technology. They were killed by questions nobody asked before the money went in.

Value: what measurable outcome does it move, and by how much? “It’ll save time” isn’t an answer. “It cuts invoice processing from four days to one, across 2,000 invoices a month” is. If nobody can name the number, the idea isn’t ready for a budget.

Test account separation, permissions, billing, AI output quality, error handling, and important user journeys. Confirm that the application can be maintained, that required credentials are under your control, and that the handover documentation is complete.

## Technical Questions to Ask Before Hiring [...] An AI SaaS developer builds software-as-a-service products that use artificial intelligence to deliver features to customers over the internet. Depending on the project, the developer may create a new product or add AI capabilities to an existing SaaS application. [...] ### 5. AI evaluation and cost control

A reliable AI product needs ways to test output quality and monitor performance. Depending on the use case, this can include evaluation datasets, human review, logging, usage limits, caching, and fallback behaviour.

### 6. Deployment and maintenance

Look for experience with automated testing, deployment workflows, error monitoring, backups, and documentation. Ask how the developer will support the product after launch and what ongoing work will cost.

In human resources, executive teams hear constant promises about automated recruiting, predictive talent planning, and effortless workforce intelligence.
